normalization.title: The $1,000 AI Workflow Is Really a Routing Problem
normalization.overview: David Ondrej’s three-day experiment is less convincing as a model leaderboard than as a demonstration of where expensive reasoning belongs, when to switch to cheaper execution, and why automation needs proof.
normalization.whyItMatters: Unaudited usage and productivity figures cannot establish that a multi-model workflow improves accepted delivery quality.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Route by uncertainty and data authorization, require task-level acceptance, and prefer scripts for deterministic checks.

archiveCall.label: Measure accepted tasks, not spend
archiveCall.text: Test matched engineering tasks for accepted delivery, human review cost and escaped defects.

normalization.falsification: Compare eight to twelve matched tasks against a strong single-model baseline using equal acceptance, latency, usage and defect measures.

Parallel coding shifts bottlenecks into review and integration.

relationshipReview.rationale: Tony explicitly approved these two distinct Reader comparisons under issue #175: routing is insufficient without authority and acceptance, while parallel code generation shifts work into review and integration. Neither link is independent source corroboration.

sharePlaneRelationships.title: The Code Is No Longer The Hard Part
sharePlaneRelationships.reason: This Work extends the distinction between generating abundant code and producing accepted engineering outcomes. It supports a comparison about review and integration cost, not a benchmark of Ondrej’s workflow.

sharePlaneRelationships.title: The Agent Is Not The Product The Control Plane Is
sharePlaneRelationships.reason: This Work provides the control-plane counterpoint: choosing an expensive reasoning model and a cheap executor cannot establish authorization, acceptance, provenance, or production safety on its own.

sharePlaneReview.rationale: Tony explicitly approved two SharePlane Work comparisons under issue #175. One extends the claim that accepted work outranks raw code output; the other supplies a counterpoint about governed authority and control planes. They remain editorial comparisons, not independent corroboration or a SharePlane graph mutation.
